validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed, independent of GEM/wiki. The pipeline is real, operating, and well documented: (1) Intergas Central Asia's own asset list (intergas.kz/ru/obwaya-informaciya, current ref for Status) lists 'МГ «Акшабулак-Кызылорда»' under its UMG (gas-transport branch) 'Кызылорда' -- i.e. it is on the company's current operating roster (this is why url_verifier's literal 'operating' substring check false-negatived: the page is in Russian and never uses the English word, but the listing itself confirms operating status by context, per url_verifier's documented STATUS-is-inferable rule). (2) Intergas.kz's own retrospective news article (intergas.kz/ru/news/5/443, current ref for Fuel/PipelineType) narrates construction and 2004 gas start-up of this exact 123-km trunk line to Kyzylorda -- read in full, it clearly names this pipeline (not a generic citation) and calls it 'магистральный газопровод' (trunk/main pipeline), which supports PipelineType=transmission and Fuel=Gas. (3) KazMunayGas's own audited annual-report gas-transportation table lists 'Akshabulak-Kyzylorda' as one of Intergas Central Asia's operating trunk pipelines in THREE consecutive vintages (AR2019, AR2020, AR2021 PDFs, all HTTP 200) with a consistent Length=123 km across all three (unlike the other 6 Intergas lines, which shrank ~20-35% between the 2020 and 2021 vintages -- this one line's length figure did NOT move, so it is not touched by that scope-redefinition artifact). (4) Kyzylorda Region's own government investment portal (kyzylorda.invest.gov.kz/ru/about/infrastructure) independently states length=123 km and describes the pipeline's purpose (associated-gas supply from South Turgay basin fields to Kyzylorda city) in terms consistent with GEM's start/end and FuelSource. (5) A Kyzylorda regional newspaper retrospective (kzvesti.kz, 2025-01-11) independently narrates the 2004 government directive (ЗАО «КазТрансГаз», May 2004) to build the line and explicitly names Akshabulak field as the associated-gas source and Intergas Central Asia's Kyzylorda UMG branch as operator -- though this ONE source gives length as '124 km' rather than 123 (a single-word narrative variance against 3+ concordant sources at 123; not treated as a material spec conflict). (6) GulfPub (Tier 2, one source) shows a clean geometry+attribute overlap for P3965 (name 1.00, endpoints 1.00, length score 0.923 at 122.31 km) -- consistent, corroborating but not independently decisive alone. CLASSIFICATION: correct as recorded -- a ~123 km trunk/transmission line from a producing gas field to a regional capital's city-gas system, explicitly called 'магистральный' (trunk) by its own operator, is transmission, not a gathering/feeder line. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 39-row Kazakhstan-gas roster -- no other row shares this name, these endpoints, or this route; not part of any flagged redundancy cluster. Not a duplicate. CAVEAT: OSM's Kazakhstan-gas extract has no matching trace for this pipeline (gem_only in the OSM recon diff) -- no geometry corroboration available from that source, and RouteAccuracy is already recorded as 'very low (straight line/schematic)', which is out of scope for this validity pass. Diameter (325 mm) could not be independently corroborated from any citable web source found this pass -- GulfPub's raw diameter field ('12.0', presumably inches) is roughly consistent with 325 mm (NPS 12 nominal OD = 323.9 mm) but GulfPub alone is Tier 2 and its own composite diff scored the diameter sub-signal 0.0 (likely a raw-unit mismatch in the automated matcher, not a real disagreement) -- left UNRESOLVED rather than fabricating a stronger claim.

validity.researcher_notes: SPEC CHECK on Capacity=0.23 bcm/y: this does NOT hold up against independent corroboration, while Length=123 km is well confirmed. Two genuinely independent sources agree with each other and disagree with GEM's capacity value: (1) KazMunayGas's own gas-transportation table gives capacity 0.42 bln m3/year in AR2021, and 0.4 bln m3/year in both AR2019 and AR2020 (all three PDFs verified 200 OK; content-substring screen false-negatived on 'Akshabulak' for the AR2021 PDF specifically -- a known false-negative pattern on large, graphic/column-heavy PDFs per url_verifier's own docstring -- so I downloaded and read it directly with `pdftotext -layout`, which shows the row 'Akshabulak-Kyzylorda 123 0.42' verbatim in the trunk-pipeline table; AR2019/AR2020 show the same row-pair '123 / 0.4'). This is ONE publisher across three vintages -- one origin. (2) Kyzylorda Region's own government investment portal (kyzylorda.invest.gov.kz/ru/about/infrastructure, independently verified) states in prose: 'Общая протяженность трассы газопровода составляет 123 км, пропускная способность 420,0 млн. куб. м газа в год' (total pipeline length 123 km, throughput capacity 420.0 million m3 of gas per year) -- a genuinely separate origin (regional government, not KMG/QazaqGaz corporate) landing on the same ~420-421 million m3/y figure. Both sources agree with each other (420-421 vs 420 vs 400, all ~0.4-0.42 bcm/y) and both disagree with GEM's 0.23 bcm/y by a wide, non-rounding margin. GulfPub's capacity field for this row is explicitly 'Not specified' in its raw data (a placeholder, not a real scraped value) and is NOT used as corroboration either way. This is a genuine spec discrepancy, not a units or vintage artifact (all vintages of the KMG table agree with each other on this specific line, unlike the other 6 Intergas lines which show a real ~20-35% cross-vintage shift) -- flagging for Update, not auto-applying.

fills.researcher_notes: StartYear1=2004 confirmed by three independent Russian-language sources: Intergas's own retrospective (gas reached Kyzylorda residents in November 2004), Kyzylorda region's government investment portal ('Газификация области началась в 2004 году со строительства... Акшабулак-Кызылорда'), and a regional newspaper retrospective (May 2004 government directive to KazTransGas to begin construction; first winter-2004 gasification of Kyzylorda tied to Independence Day).

123 km confirmed by KMG's own gas-transportation table (all 3 vintages, one publisher), Kyzylorda's government investment portal ('составляет 123 км', independent origin), and Intergas's own retrospective news article. GulfPub (Tier 2) independently lands within 1% (122.31 km, route IoU low but attribute match strong). One weaker outlier: a regional newspaper retrospective gives 124 km -- not treated as a material conflict given the 3+ concordant sources at 123. AR2021 PDF's 'Akshabulak' token false-negatived on url_verifier's content screen (large graphic-column PDF, documented false-negative pattern); confirmed manually with `pdftotext -layout`, row reads 'Akshabulak-Kyzylorda 123 0.42' verbatim.

kzvesti.kz explicitly names 'месторождение Акшабулак' as the source of the associated gas transported by this pipeline to Kyzylorda. Kyzylorda's government portal is less specific ('месторождений Южно-Тургайской впадины' -- South Turgay basin fields, plural), consistent with but not naming Akshabulak alone, so kept at medium tier rather than high.

Both endpoints and Kyzylorda Region attribution confirmed by Kyzylorda's own regional government portal (which treats the pipeline as an in-region asset feeding the oblast capital from South Turgay basin fields) and Intergas's retrospective, both independent of GEM/wiki.

Intergas Central Asia's own asset list places 'МГ «Акшабулак-Кызылорда»' under its Kyzylorda UMG (gas-transport branch). Independently, kzvesti.kz explicitly states the pipeline is operated via 'филиал управления магистральных газопроводов (УМГ) «Кызылорда» АО «Интергаз Центральная Азия»'. tab=operators_owners.

QazaqGaz's own current corporate-structure page lists 'Intergas Central Asia JSC' under 'Trunk transportation' in its group of companies -- i.e. ICA is a QazaqGaz subsidiary today. AR2021 (pre-Nov-2021 spinoff of the gas arm from KMG to Samruk-Kazyna/QazaqGaz) independently states 'JSC Intergas Central Asia (ICA) is the national gas pipeline operator and a wholly-owned subsidiary of KTG [KazTransGas]' with 'Interest: KTG: 100%'. The two sources describe the same 100%-state-owned chain across the Nov-2021 corporate reorganization (KTG/KMG group -> QazaqGaz/Samruk-Kazyna group); GEM's Owner1=QazaqGaz 100% reflects the current (post-reorg) parent correctly. GulfPub's owner field for this row ('QazaqGaz') cites the same qazaqgaz.kz page, so it is not counted as a second independent source.
